tour.name: 8-Day Private Turkey Highlights Tour: Istanbul, Cappadocia, Pamukkale & Ephesus
tour.subtitle: The great journey through Turkey with licensed guides and private cars: the mosques, palaces and bazaars of Istanbul and a Bosphorus cruise, two nights in a Cappadocia cave hotel, the Seljuk caravanserai of Sultanhanı and Rumi's tomb in Konya, the white travertines of Pamukkale and the marble streets of Ephesus.
tour.seoTitle: 8-Day Private Turkey Tour: Istanbul to Ephesus | TRAVSUS
tour.metaDescription: Private 8-day Turkey tour: Istanbul, Bosphorus cruise, Cappadocia cave hotel, Konya, Pamukkale and Ephesus with licensed guides, private cars, 7 nights' hotels, domestic flight and tickets.
highlights: Hagia Sophia, the Blue Mosque, Topkapı Palace and the Basilica Cistern
A private cruise on the Bosphorus between Europe and Asia
Two nights in a cave hotel in Göreme, Cappadocia
The Göreme Open Air Museum and Kaymaklı underground city
Rumi's green-domed tomb in Konya and the Sultanhanı caravanserai
The white travertines and Roman spa city of Pamukkale
The Library of Celsus and the Terrace Houses of Ephesus
tour.overview:
Turkey is where Europe and Asia meet, and where Greeks, Romans, Byzantines, Seljuks and Ottomans each left some of their greatest monuments. This private journey crosses the country from the Bosphorus to the Aegean in eight days, with a licensed guide at every stop, private cars and drivers, carefully chosen hotels and one domestic flight to save a long day on the road.

You begin with two and a half days in Istanbul: Hagia Sophia, the Blue Mosque, Topkapı Palace, the Basilica Cistern and the Grand Bazaar, then a private cruise on the Bosphorus and the Spice Bazaar. A short flight takes you to Cappadocia for two nights in a cave hotel, with dawn balloons, frescoed rock churches, fairy chimneys and an underground city. You then follow the old Silk Road west, through the Seljuk caravanserai of Sultanhanı to Konya and the tomb of the poet Rumi. From there you cross the lake district to Pamukkale, where you walk barefoot on the white travertines above Hierapolis, and finish in Ephesus, the best-preserved Roman city of the eastern Mediterranean, before your flight home from Izmir.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: 8 days, 7 nights
• Start: Istanbul airport (IST or SAW)
• End: Izmir airport (ADB)
• Type: private tour with licensed guides, cars and drivers; 7 nights in hotels with breakfast; domestic flight Istanbul to Cappadocia
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability, hotels, flights and final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy to moderate; daily walks of 3 to 6 km, some uneven ground and steps

WHAT YOU SEE
• Istanbul: Hagia Sophia, the Blue Mosque, Topkapı Palace, the Basilica Cistern, the Grand Bazaar, the Bosphorus and the Spice Bazaar.
• Cappadocia: Uçhisar, the Göreme Open Air Museum, Paşabağ, Avanos, Rose Valley and Kaymaklı underground city.
• Sultanhanı caravanserai and the Mevlana Museum in Konya.
• Pamukkale travertines and Hierapolis.
• Ephesus, the Terrace Houses, the House of the Virgin Mary and the Temple of Artemis.

WHY THIS WORKS
One flight from Istanbul to Cappadocia saves a 10-hour drive, while the drive west through Konya and the lakes breaks the long road into two scenic days with real stops. Each place gets enough time to be enjoyed, not just seen.

WHO IT SUITS
First-time visitors to Turkey, couples, families and small groups who want the classic sights with private guiding and no shopping stops.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you prefer to stay in one place, choose our 3-day Cappadocia tour or our Istanbul day tours. The drive days (days 5 and 6) are 4 to 5 hours each.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
The balloon flight in Cappadocia is optional and not included. Hagia Sophia and the Blue Mosque are active mosques: women need a headscarf and everyone must cover shoulders and knees. Pack layers: Cappadocia is cooler than the coast.

days.name: Arrival in Istanbul and the Hippodrome at dusk
days.description:
What to expect: a private airport welcome, check-in near the old city and a gentle first evening walk.

Your driver meets you at Istanbul Airport (about 50 minutes from the old city) or Sabiha Gökçen Airport (about 1 hour 15 minutes) and takes you to your hotel in or near Sultanahmet. If you arrive by mid-afternoon, your guide meets you for a short walk around the Hippodrome, the Roman and Byzantine racecourse where chariots once raced before 100,000 spectators. Today it is a long square with an Egyptian obelisk of Thutmose III brought by Theodosius in 390, the bronze Serpent Column from Delphi and the German Fountain. As the light fades, the domes and minarets of the Blue Mosque and Hagia Sophia are lit up, and the call to prayer echoes across the square. Your guide gives you a briefing on the days ahead and recommends a restaurant for dinner.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
Any time – Airport welcome and transfer to your hotel.
17:00 – Evening walk around the Hippodrome and Sultanahmet Square (about 1 hour).
18:00 – Free evening.

GOOD TO KNOW
• If you arrive late, the evening walk is moved to day 2 or 3.
• Turkish lira is useful for small purchases; cards are widely accepted.

INCLUDED: airport transfer, licensed guide for the evening walk.
NOT INCLUDED: dinner, drinks, tips.

Overnight: hotel in Istanbul (Sultanahmet).
Meals: none.

days.name: Istanbul old city: Hagia Sophia, Blue Mosque, Basilica Cistern, Topkapı and the Grand Bazaar
days.description:
What to expect: a full day in the historic peninsula with your licensed guide, covering 1,600 years of Byzantine and Ottoman history.

You start early at Hagia Sophia, completed in 537 under Emperor Justinian, whose dome seemed to float above the largest interior in the world for nearly a thousand years. It was a cathedral, then a mosque from 1453, a museum from 1934 and again a mosque since 2020; visitors now see it from the upper gallery, where the Byzantine mosaics of Christ, the Virgin and the emperors are closest. Across the square, the Blue Mosque (Sultan Ahmed Mosque), finished in 1616, takes its name from the more than 20,000 blue İznik tiles inside. Below ground, the Basilica Cistern, built by Justinian, holds 336 columns standing in water, including two resting on Medusa heads.

After lunch you visit Topkapı Palace, the home of the Ottoman sultans for almost 400 years: its courtyards, kitchens, treasury with the Spoonmaker's Diamond, the sacred relics and the terraces over the Bosphorus. The Harem is optional. You end the day in the Grand Bazaar, one of the oldest and largest covered markets in the world, with more than 4,000 shops along 60 streets, where your guide shows you the old inns and the best places for tea, lamps, ceramics and textiles – with no commission shops.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
08:30 – Departure from your hotel on foot.
08:45 – Hagia Sophia (about 1 hour).
10:00 – Blue Mosque (outside prayer times).
11:00 – Basilica Cistern.
12:15 – Lunch.
13:30 – Topkapı Palace (about 2 hours 30 minutes).
16:30 – Grand Bazaar.
17:30 – Return to your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Topkapı is closed on Tuesdays and the Grand Bazaar on Sundays; we arrange the days around them.
• The Blue Mosque closes to visitors during the five daily prayers, longer on Friday at midday.
• Women need a headscarf in mosques; we bring spare scarves.

INCLUDED: licensed guide, tickets to Hagia Sophia, the Basilica Cistern and Topkapı Palace, lunch, bottled water.
NOT INCLUDED: Harem ticket, dinner, drinks, tips.

Overnight: hotel in Istanbul (Sultanahmet).
Meals: breakfast, lunch.

days.name: Bosphorus cruise, Spice Bazaar and flight to Cappadocia
days.description:
What to expect: a private boat on the strait between Europe and Asia, the scents of the Spice Bazaar and an evening flight to Cappadocia.

After breakfast you board a private boat near Eminönü for a two-hour cruise up the Bosphorus, the 30-km strait that links the Black Sea and the Sea of Marmara and divides Istanbul between two continents. You glide past the white marble façade of Dolmabahçe Palace, the baroque Ortaköy Mosque beneath the first Bosphorus bridge, the wooden yalı mansions of Ottoman families, and the towers of Rumelihisarı, the fortress built by Mehmed II in 1452 to prepare the conquest of Constantinople. Your guide points out which shore is Europe and which is Asia, and how the city lives on the water.

Back on land, you walk through the Spice Bazaar, built in the 1660s as part of the New Mosque complex, among pyramids of spices, dried fruit, Turkish delight and teas, and have lunch nearby. In the afternoon your driver takes you to the airport for the flight of about 1 hour 20 minutes to Kayseri or Nevşehir. Your Cappadocia driver meets you and takes you to your cave hotel in Göreme.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
09:30 – Private Bosphorus cruise from Eminönü (about 2 hours).
11:45 – Spice Bazaar.
12:45 – Lunch.
14:30 – Transfer to the airport.
17:00 – Flight to Kayseri or Nevşehir.
19:30 – Arrival at your cave hotel in Göreme.

GOOD TO KNOW
• The flight time may vary; we adapt the morning to it.
• Luggage allowance on domestic flights is usually 15 to 20 kg; we will tell you yours.

INCLUDED: private Bosphorus cruise, licensed guide, lunch, domestic flight, transfers in Istanbul and Cappadocia.
NOT INCLUDED: dinner, extra luggage, drinks, tips.

Overnight: cave hotel in Göreme.
Meals: breakfast, lunch.

days.name: Cappadocia: balloons, Göreme Open Air Museum, Paşabağ, Avanos, Uçhisar and Rose Valley
days.description:
What to expect: the balloons at dawn, the frescoed rock churches, fairy chimneys, potters and a sunset walk.

If you have booked a balloon flight, you are collected before sunrise and float over the valleys for about an hour. Otherwise, step out onto your hotel terrace to watch dozens of balloons rise around Göreme. After breakfast your Cappadocia guide takes you to the Göreme Open Air Museum, a monastic complex of rock-cut churches and refectories used from the 10th to the 12th centuries, with frescoes of the life of Christ in bright blues and reds; the Tokalı Church is included and the Dark Church can be added.

You continue to Paşabağ, the Monks Valley, where fairy chimneys with two or three caps rise like giant mushrooms, and to Avanos on the Red River, where potters have shaped its red clay since the Hittites. After lunch you climb Uçhisar castle, the highest point in the region, for a view over the whole landscape, then begin an easy walk of about 3 km through Rose Valley, past hidden churches and pink cliffs, ending at a viewpoint for sunset.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
05:00 – Optional balloon flight.
09:00 – Göreme Open Air Museum.
11:00 – Paşabağ (Monks Valley).
12:00 – Pottery workshop in Avanos and lunch.
14:30 – Uçhisar castle.
16:00 – Rose Valley walk and sunset.
18:30 – Return to your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Balloon flights are decided each morning by the civil aviation authority; if yours is cancelled, we try again on day 5.
• There is no obligation to buy at the pottery workshop.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, licensed guide, tickets to the Göreme Open Air Museum, Paşabağ and Uçhisar, lunch, bottled water.
NOT INCLUDED: balloon flight, Dark Church, dinner, drinks, tips.

Overnight: cave hotel in Göreme.
Meals: breakfast, lunch.

days.name: Kaymaklı underground city, Sultanhanı caravanserai and Konya
days.description:
What to expect: a descent into an underground city, a great Seljuk caravanserai and the tomb of Rumi.

After breakfast, with a back-up balloon morning if needed, you drive about 20 minutes to Kaymaklı, one of the largest underground cities in Cappadocia. Begun perhaps in Phrygian times and greatly extended under the Byzantines, its levels of tunnels, stables, kitchens, chapels and ventilation shafts sheltered villagers for weeks during raids, and its rolling stone doors could be closed from inside.

You then head west on the old Silk Road across the high plateau, with the snow-capped volcano Hasan to the south. At Sultanhanı you stop at one of the largest Seljuk caravanserais in Anatolia, built in 1229 under Sultan Kayqubad I, where merchants and their camels found shelter, water and a small mosque behind a magnificent carved portal. In the afternoon you reach Konya, the Seljuk capital, and visit the Mevlana Museum, the tomb of the 13th-century poet and mystic Jalaluddin Rumi beneath its turquoise-tiled dome, with the former lodge of the whirling dervishes, their musical instruments and illuminated manuscripts.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
05:00 – Back-up balloon morning if needed.
08:30 – Check-out and Kaymaklı underground city.
10:30 – Drive west (about 2 hours).
12:30 – Sultanhanı caravanserai, then lunch.
14:30 – Drive to Konya (about 1 hour 15 minutes).
16:00 – Mevlana Museum.
17:30 – Check-in at your hotel in Konya.

GOOD TO KNOW
• On some Saturday evenings the Mevlana Cultural Centre holds a sema, the whirling ceremony; we will tell you if it falls on your date.
• Konya is a conservative city: dress modestly in the museum, which is also a place of pilgrimage.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, licensed guide, tickets to Kaymaklı and Sultanhanı, lunch, bottled water.
NOT INCLUDED: dinner, drinks, tips.

days.name: Through the lake district to Pamukkale: Hierapolis and the travertines at sunset
days.description:
What to expect: a scenic drive west and an afternoon on the white terraces of Pamukkale.

You leave Konya after breakfast for the drive of about 5 hours to Pamukkale, through the lake district of Anatolia, with a lunch stop by the waters of Lake Eğirdir, framed by mountains, where the old town sits on a narrow peninsula. You reach Pamukkale in the mid-afternoon and drive up to the north gate of Hierapolis, the Greek and Roman spa city founded in the 2nd century BC.

Your guide leads you through one of the largest ancient cemeteries in Anatolia and along Frontinus Street to the Domitian Gate, then up to the great Roman theatre with its carved stage building. You may swim in the Antique Pool among fallen marble columns (separate ticket). As the sun goes down, you take off your shoes and walk barefoot down the white travertines, formed by warm, calcium-rich springs, while the pools turn pink and gold. The site is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Your hotel is in the village below.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
08:30 – Departure from Konya.
12:00 – Lunch by Lake Eğirdir.
15:00 – Arrival at the north gate of Hierapolis.
15:15 – The necropolis, Frontinus Street and the Roman theatre.
17:00 – Free time at the Antique Pool or the museum.
18:00 – Sunset walk down the travertines.
19:00 – Check-in at your hotel in Pamukkale.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Shoes are not allowed on the travertines; bring a bag for them.
• In winter the sun sets earlier, so we leave Konya earlier.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, licensed guide, ticket to Pamukkale-Hierapolis, lunch, bottled water.
NOT INCLUDED: Antique Pool ticket, dinner, drinks, tips.

days.name: Ephesus, the Terrace Houses and Şirince
days.description:
What to expect: the best-preserved Roman city of the eastern Mediterranean, its painted houses and a hill village.

After breakfast you drive about 3 hours west to Ephesus, once the capital of the Roman province of Asia and a port of perhaps 250,000 people. Your guide starts at the upper gate and leads you downhill along the marble streets as the Romans knew them: the State Agora and Odeon, Curetes Street with the Temple of Hadrian and the public latrines, and the covered Terrace Houses, where wealthy families lived among frescoes and mosaics.

At the foot of Curetes Street stands the Library of Celsus, built around 117 AD by a son in honour of his father, whose two-storey façade is the most famous image of Ephesus. You walk on along the Marble Road to the Great Theatre, where, according to the Acts of the Apostles, Paul's preaching caused the riot of the silversmiths. In the late afternoon you drive up to Şirince, a hill village of whitewashed Greek houses known for its fruit wines, before checking in to your hotel in Selçuk.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
08:30 – Departure from Pamukkale.
11:30 – Lunch near Selçuk.
13:00 – Ephesus from the upper gate: Curetes Street and the Temple of Hadrian.
14:15 – Terrace Houses (about 45 minutes).
15:00 – Library of Celsus and the Great Theatre.
16:30 – Şirince village.
18:00 – Check-in at your hotel in Selçuk.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Polished marble is slippery: wear shoes with good grip.
• In summer we visit Ephesus later in the afternoon, when the cruise groups have left.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, licensed guide, tickets to Ephesus and the Terrace Houses, lunch, bottled water.
NOT INCLUDED: wine tasting, dinner, drinks, tips.

days.name: House of the Virgin Mary, Temple of Artemis and departure from Izmir
days.description:
What to expect: a pilgrimage site in the pines, the last column of a Wonder of the World and your transfer to the airport.

In the morning you drive up Mount Koressos to the House of the Virgin Mary, a small stone chapel in the pine forest where, according to tradition, Mary spent her last years; it is a place of prayer for Christians and Muslims alike. Back in Selçuk, you see the single column that remains of the Temple of Artemis, one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World, and, time permitting, the Basilica of Saint John on the hill or the Ephesus Museum with its famous statues of Artemis.

After a farewell lunch, your driver takes you to Izmir Adnan Menderes Airport, about 1 hour away, for your flight home. If you have more time, we can extend your stay on the Aegean coast.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)

11:00 – Basilica of Saint John or Ephesus Museum.

14:00 – Transfer to Izmir airport.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Choose a flight from Izmir after 16:30; for earlier flights we shorten the morning.
• Photography is not allowed inside the chapel of the House of the Virgin Mary.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, licensed guide, ticket to the House of the Virgin Mary, lunch, bottled water, airport transfer.
NOT INCLUDED: Basilica of Saint John or Ephesus Museum tickets, international flights, drinks, tips.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability, hotels, flights and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Is the domestic flight included?
faq.answer: Yes, an economy flight from Istanbul to Kayseri or Nevşehir with standard luggage. International flights to Istanbul and from Izmir are not included.

faq.question: What kind of hotels are used?
faq.answer: Comfortable boutique or 4-star hotels: a hotel in Sultanahmet in Istanbul, a cave hotel in Göreme, a city hotel in Konya, a thermal hotel in Pamukkale and a small hotel in Selçuk. Upgrades to 5-star hotels are available.

faq.question: Is the balloon flight included?
faq.answer: No, because its price varies with the season and it depends on the weather. We can book it for day 4, with day 5 as a back-up, and add it to your confirmation.

faq.question: Will we have the same guide throughout?
faq.answer: You have a licensed local guide in each region – Istanbul, Cappadocia and the Aegean – who knows their area best. Your driver accompanies you from Cappadocia to Izmir.

faq.question: Can we start or end elsewhere?
faq.answer: Yes. You can reverse the route, start from Izmir, end in Istanbul with a flight back, or add nights on the coast.

faq.question: Are the driving days long?
faq.answer: Days 5 and 6 include about 4 to 5 hours of driving each, broken by visits and lunch. The other days have short drives.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children love the underground city, the balloons, the travertines and the Roman theatres. We can add family rooms and shorten visits.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Partly. Most sites involve uneven ground and steps. Tell us your needs and we will adapt the walking and choose suitable hotels.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Comfortable shoes with grip, layers for cool Cappadocia evenings, a headscarf for women and clothes covering shoulders and knees for mosques.

faq.question: Will we be taken to shops?
faq.answer: No commission shops. The only workshop is the pottery in Avanos, a cultural visit with no obligation to buy.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: April to June and September to November. Summers are hot on the coast; winters are cold and snowy in Cappadocia and Konya but quiet everywhere.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 14 days before the tour starts; the domestic flight may be non-refundable once ticketed. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
